meta.title: Catholic Rosaries UK | Handmade rosaries
meta.description: Handmade, wire-linked rosaries made in Manchester. Find the silence in your heart, in the busyness of daily life.

hero.logoAlt: Catholic Rosaries UK logo: Our Lady with eyes closed in prayer, surrounded by rose-pink rays

variants.heading: Find the *silence* in your heart, in the busyness of daily life.
variants.lead: There’s no need to wait for a quiet hour. One decade, prayed on the way to whatever comes next, is enough to turn the heart back to God.

variants.heading: A *quiet moment* with Our Lady, wherever the day takes you.
variants.lead: God is not only found in the quiet hours. He is in the office, the traffic and the kitchen too, and the Rosary is one way to meet Him there.

variants.heading: Take *Our Lady* with you into the ordinary day.
variants.lead: At Nazareth she kept all these things in her heart, among the work of an ordinary home. Pray with her wherever your day takes you.

variants.heading: *Pray* without ceasing.
variants.lead: St Paul’s counsel was never meant only for monks and nuns. For most of us it begins with a decade on the bus or a Hail Mary at the desk.

variants.heading: Prayer in the middle of *everyday life*
intro: Most of us don’t live in a monastery. Our days are full of work, family, traffic and noise. Being a contemplative in action means finding God there, in the middle of it all, rather than waiting for a quiet moment that never comes.

A rosary is a small, practical way to do that. It sits in a pocket or bag, and a single decade fits into a commute or the minutes before a meeting. With the beads in your hand, you can find that inner silence wherever you are.

variants.heading: Finding God in the *ordinary*
intro: Few of us are called to the cloister. Our days are taken up with work, family and the many small demands of ordinary life. To be a contemplative in action is to seek God there, in the thick of it, rather than waiting for a quiet hour that rarely comes.

The Rosary suits a life like that. It asks only for a few minutes and a willing heart, and a single decade can be prayed on the train or before a meeting. With the beads in hand, even a noisy day can hold a place for prayer.

paragraphs: About four years ago, while running the piety shop at my parish, I grew tired of rosaries that came apart too easily and offered little beyond plastic beads and plain medals. Making my own began as a practical answer and became something I love. There is something in the patient work of closing each link that feels like prayer: small joins, one after another, holding the whole together. I hope each rosary helps someone come closer to the Lord.
St Teresa found the Lord among the pots and pans. These rosaries are made for that kind of life: linked with wire rather than cord, finished with care, and strong enough to stay with you for years.

items.title: Five-decade rosaries
items.text: The traditional five-decade rosary, with a detailed centre medal and crucifix, for praying the mysteries in full.

items.title: Car tenners
items.text: A single decade with a clasp, to hang from the mirror, attach to steering wheel or keep in the glovebox.

items.title: Keychains
items.text: A few beads and a medal on a key ring, for your keys or the handle of a bag.

beads.heading: Stone, glass or *wood*
beads.intro: Beads have been used to count prayers for centuries. I choose materials that sit well in the hand and will last through years of use.

items.title: Agate
items.text: A banded quartz that forms slowly, layer on layer, so no two beads are quite alike. It’s hard and resists scratching, which makes it one of the most durable stones for a rosary.

items.title: Amazonite
items.text: A green to blue-green stone, often with fine white streaks, so each bead has its own markings. It’s mined in places as far apart as Brazil, Russia and Madagascar.

items.title: Glass pearl
items.text: A solid glass core with a pearl finish, heavier and smoother than plastic, with a soft sheen. At this size the beads are tough and stand up well to everyday handling.

items.title: Wood
items.text: The oldest and simplest material for prayer beads. It’s light and warm in the hand and mellows with use. Keep it dry. More woods to come.
slimmer and lighter. Sits neatly in a pocket.
fuller in the hand and easier to count by touch.

medals.heading: Medals and *devotions*
medals.intro: Each medal carries a devotion of its own, with its own history and its own prayer. The one at the centre of a rosary often reflects something of the person who prays with it.

items.title: The Miraculous Medal
items.text: Made to the design Our Lady gave St Catherine Labouré in 1830, with the prayer “O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.”

items.title: St Michael the Archangel
items.text: Protector in spiritual battle, and patron of police, soldiers and the sick. A lovely gift of protection.

items.title: The Holy Face
items.text: Shows the Face of Jesus as on Veronica’s veil, with the prayer “Let the light of your face shine upon us, O Lord.” A devotion of love and reparation to Christ.

pray.heading: Praying the Rosary
pray.intro: The Rosary walks through the life of Christ alongside Mary. Each decade has a mystery to reflect on as you pray. Pray all five decades, or just one when that’s all the day allows.

steps.heading: How to pray it
items: On the crucifix, make the Sign of the Cross and say the Apostles’ Creed.
On the first bead, an Our Father. On the next three, a Hail Mary each, then a Glory Be.
Announce the first mystery, then pray an Our Father on the single bead.
Pray ten Hail Marys on the decade, then a Glory Be and the Fatima Prayer.
Repeat for the other four decades, and finish with the Hail, Holy Queen at the centre medal.

mysteries.heading: The mysteries, by day

items.name: Joyful

items.name: Glorious
list: The Descent of the Holy Spirit

mysteries.note: Your rosary can also be used for chaplets prayed on five decades, such as the Divine Mercy Chaplet.

items.title: The Sign of the Cross
lines: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

items.title: The Apostles’ Creed
lines: I believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth,
and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary,
suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried;
he descended into hell; on the third day he rose again from the dead;
he ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church,
the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting. Amen.

items.title: Our Father
lines: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name;
thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread,
and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us;
and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

items.title: Hail Mary
lines: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee;
blessed art thou among women,
and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners,
now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

items.title: Glory Be
lines: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit;
as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be,
world without end. Amen.

items.title: The Fatima Prayer
lines: O my Jesus, forgive us our sins,
save us from the fires of hell;
lead all souls to heaven,
especially those in most need of thy mercy.

items.title: Hail, Holy Queen
lines: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, hail, our life, our sweetness and our hope.
To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve;
to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears.
Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us,
and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
V. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
